- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward trends), apply a 3–5% downward bias to the forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to negative or vice versa), adjust forecast to align with the sentiment shift, especially in the first 7–10 days of the forecast horizon.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if forecast is above 3 standard deviations from recent mean, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly supports it.
